name: OH-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Balderson's large financial advantage ($2.0M vs $19K cash)
No polls or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Balderson: a heavily Republican seat, incumbency, and a roughly 20-to-1 cash advantage over Christian, with markets pricing a Republican win near certainty. Nothing in the evidence justifies moving materially from the baseline margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or polling showing Christian within single digits would warrant rethinking.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Troy Balderson seeks another term in a central Ohio district that leans strongly Republican, with a partisan advantage of about fifteen points. He enters the general election with roughly $2 million on hand after raising $1.7 million, while Democrat Jerrad Christian has raised under $85,000 and holds about $19,000. No independent polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 95 percent chance of winning.

The forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture, all of which favor Balderson by a wide margin. Christian would need a dramatic shift in the political environment or a major influx of resources to make this competitive, and there is no evidence of either so far.
